rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone reads al-ghudwah, treating the word as the named time without the ordinary article.
rows.anchor: ابن عامر وحده: (بالغدوة والعشي)

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use al-ghadāh; the author considers this form clearer.
rows.anchor: الباقون: بالغداة والعشي بألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although ghudwah is a proper name, it may be generalized and take the article; spelling it with wāw proves no wāw sound, as in الصلاة.
rows.anchor: أما غدوة فهو اسم موضوع للتعريف، وإذا كان كذلك

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: All readers except Ibn ʿĀmir read the third-person indicative يَشْرِكُ, continuing the preceding references to an absent subject; God does not share His judgment with anyone.
rows.anchor: وكلهم قرأ: ولا يشرك في حكمه أحدا

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads the second-person jussive prohibition, addressing a person: do not associate anyone in God's judgment.
rows.anchor: غير ابن عامر فإنه قرأ: (ولا تشرك) جزما بالتاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The third-person reading is more widespread; the shift from divine absence to direct address is also idiomatic, as in the change to إياك نعبد.
rows.anchor: والقراءة الأولى أشيع، والرجوع من الغيبة إلى الخطاب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains the final yāʾ in the listed forms in both connection and pause, which the author calls the original analogical form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير: (إن ترني أنا) [الكهف/ 39]

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr retain yāʾ in connection for their listed forms, add المهتدي, and omit it at pauses because these endings resemble rhyme.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو بياء في الوصل في هذه الحروف

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī omits the yāʾ generally but retains it in نبغي when connected.
rows.anchor: الكسائي يحذفها ويثبت الياء في (نبغي) وحدها في الوصل

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, ʿĀṣim, and Ḥamzah omit these yāʾs in both connection and pause; in connection they also omit yāʾ in non-rhyme forms such as يوم يأت.
rows.anchor: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة يحذفون الياء في الوصل والوقف

rows.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر والكسائي
rows.claim: Abū Bakr's transmission from ʿĀṣim and al-Kisāʾī read turḍā with a ḍamma on tāʾ.
rows.anchor: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر والكسائي: (لعلك ترضى)

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The remaining readers, including the familiar transmission from Ḥafṣ, read tarḍā with fatḥa on tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون، وهبيرة عن حفص عن عاصم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The fatḥa reading is supported by the promise that the Prophet will be pleased; the ḍamma reading evokes the description of a prophet as pleasing to God and can mean being pleased with obedience or God's gift of a high rank.
rows.anchor: حجة من فتح التاء قوله: ولسوف يعطيك ربك فترضى

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Al-Bazzī's transmission from Ibn Kathīr has an imperative at the question and a reported statement at the answer; Qunbul's cited transmission has imperatives at both places.
rows.anchor: فقرأ ابن كثير: (قل كم لبثتم) على الأمر قال إن على الخبر

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers use قال at both locations, presenting both clauses as reports rather than commands.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر: قال كم لبثتم

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamzah and al-Kisāʾī read قل at both locations, addressing the questioner with an imperative; the Kufan codex reading قل supports their choice.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي: (قل كم لبثتم) و (قل إن لبثتم)

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers assimilate thāʾ into tāʾ because their articulation points are close and both are voiceless; Ibn Kathīr favors clear separation because the articulation points differ.
rows.anchor: وأبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي يدغمون التاء، الباقون لا يدغمون

rows.speaker: ورش عن نافع
rows.claim: Warsh from Nāfiʿ reads يؤلف without pronouncing the hamza, replacing the softened hamza with wāw.
rows.anchor: ورش عن نافع: لا يهمز يولف [النور/ 43]

rows.speaker: قالون والباقون
rows.claim: Qālūn and the other readers pronounce the hamza; both forms are acceptable because the word derives from joining things and Arabic regularly softens this hamza to wāw.
rows.anchor: إذا كان من: ألفت بين الشيئين، إذا جمعت

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir alone has a still sīn in كسفا; the other readers open it.
rows.anchor: كلهم قرأ : ويجعله كسفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opened form can be parsed like sidrah/sidr, with the same meaning as كسف; the following pronoun may refer either to the fragments or to the cloud, while the other vocalization points to the cloud alone.
rows.anchor: الكسف القطع، الواحدة كسفة، مثل: سدرة وسدر

rows.speaker: عاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim and Ḥamzah read all three occurrences with fatḥa on ḍād; the other readers use ḍamma, including Ḥafṣ in the cited report.
rows.anchor: فقرأ عاصم وحمزة من ضعف بفتح الضاد فيهن كلهن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two vocalizations are dialectal synonyms, comparable to the two forms for poverty; weakness here means creation from weak fluid.
rows.anchor: هما لغتان ومثله: الفقر والفقر،

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports reciting the phrase before the Prophet, who repeated it with the ḍamma form.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر أنه قال: قرأت على رسول الله

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamzah reads ننكسه with a doubled k, while ʿĀṣim's transmissions are mixed: most cited transmitters double it, but Hubayrah and ʿAlī ibn Naṣr report a light k.
rows.anchor: فقرأ حمزة: ننكسه مشددا، واختلف عن عاصم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah explains the reversal as aging until a person knows nothing after having knowledge.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: ننكسه في الخلق لكي لا يعلم بعد علم شيئا

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Another explanation is that prolonged life turns strength into weakness and youth into old age.
rows.anchor: غيره، معناه: من أطلنا عمره نكسنا خلقه، فصار بدل القوة ضعفا

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan calls ننكسه ordinary Arabic usage; he says نكسته is usually reserved for turning something upside down, and another authority reports that Abū ʿAmr rejected this form.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: ننكسه، وهو كلام العرب، قال

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Abū ʿAmr in the transmission from ʿAbbās read أفلا تعقلون in the second person, addressing the hearers.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وأبو عمرو في رواية عباس بن الفضل عنه: أفلا تعقلون

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use the third-person أفلا يعقلون, meaning, 'Tell them: do they not reason?'; the second person continues the address in the preceding verse.
rows.anchor: وجه الياء على: قل لهم: أفلا يعقلون

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah takes فلا أقسم as فأقسم and مواقع النجوم as their settings, where the stars disappear.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم أي: فأقسم، قال

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the مواقع the successive places where the Qur'an descended to the Prophet; the phrase can also connect to the oath by the star in 53:1.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنه مواقع القرآن حين نزل على النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم نجوما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A verbal noun or generic noun may be singular for one kind and plural when its instances differ; this explains singular موقع versus plural مواقع.
rows.anchor: فمن قال: بموقع فأفرد، فلأنه اسم جنس، ومن جمع، فلاختلاف ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the cited verse, مواقع الطير means multiple places rather than a verbal noun, so its plural reflects the several bird perches.
rows.anchor: كأن متني من النقي مواقع الطير على الصفي

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr alone reads وأكون with wāw; he coordinates the verb with the visible, subjunctive form فأصدق.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو وحده: وأكون [المنافقين/ 10] بواو

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers read وأكن without wāw, coordinating it with فأصدق's underlying jussive position as the response to an implied condition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون: وأكن بغير واو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both syntactic attachments are defensible: one follows the underlying jussive position and the other the expressed wording; the verse means, 'Delay me and I will give charity.'
rows.anchor: أخرني أصدق، كان جزما بأنه جواب الجزاء

rows.speaker: عاصم في رواية أبي بكر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr's transmission from ʿĀṣim reads يعملون in the third person; the prior singular النفس can represent many people, licensing agreement by meaning.
rows.anchor: قرأ عاصم في رواية أبي بكر: والله خبير بما يعملون بالياء

rows.speaker: الباقون وحفص عن عاصم
rows.claim: The other readers, including Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim, address the audience directly with تعملون.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون وحفص عن عاصم بالتاء

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ and Ibn ʿĀmir read both verbs with first-person plural nūn, speaking of God's forgiveness and admission into the gardens.
rows.anchor: قرأ نافع وابن عامر: نكفر عنه سيئاته وندخله [9] بالنون جميعا

rows.speaker: الباقون
rows.claim: The other readers use third-person يَدْخُلْهُ, returning to the explicit preceding subject; the nūn shift is supported by a similar shift in the account of Moses.
rows.anchor: حجة الياء: أن الاسم الظاهر قد تقدم

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم وابن عامر والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers say دَبَرَ with fatḥa on dāl, the form Yunus glosses as having passed or ended.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو وأبو بكر عن عاصم وابن عامر

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم في رواية حفص وحمزة
rows.claim: These readers say أَدْبَرَ with a still dāl; Yunus distinguishes it as having turned away.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم في رواية حفص وحمزة: والليل إذ أدبر

rows.speaker: يونس
rows.claim: Yunus distinguishes دبر, 'ended,' from أدبر, 'turned away,' while also explaining the phrases about the stars and prostrations as their decline or aftermath.
rows.anchor: ابن سلام عن يونس قال يونس: دبر: انقضى، وأدبر: تولى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan interprets the setting of the stars as the two dawn rakʿahs and the aftermath of prostration as two rakʿahs after sunset; reports from Mujāhid and Ibn ʿAbbās illustrate the phrase as night turns away.
rows.anchor: ذكر غير واحد من أصحاب الحديث عن الحسن أنه قال: إدبار النجوم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah explains the night as having departed, and the poet's expression 'yesterday that had passed' supports both forms.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: والليل إذا دبر: إذا ولى

rows.speaker: قنبل عن ابن كثير
rows.claim: Qunbul from Ibn Kathīr pronounces the hamza in لإحدى, like Abū ʿAmr; another report from Ibn Kathīr omits it altogether.
rows.anchor: قنبل عن ابن كثير: إنها لإحدى الكبر [المدثر/ 35] مهموز

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah identifies the great calamity as Hell.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: إنها لإحدى الكبر: جهنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regular easing places the hamza between hamza and vowel; outright deletion is non-analogical, though poetic elision supplies precedents, including al-Farazdaq's إثم.
rows.anchor: فأما حذف الهمزة فليس بقياس، ووجه ذلك أن الهمزة حذفت حذفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Deleting the hamza is especially weak because it leaves a word-initial consonant cluster, but the attached lām makes the word behave internally, like a single word with an eased hamza.
rows.anchor: ولهذا لم يتخفف الهمزة أولا، لأن التخفيف تقريب من الساكن

rows.speaker: من نون
rows.claim: The tanwīn reading treats مُنذِرٌ as a present participle denoting a current warning, supported by the parallel present warning in 21:45.
rows.anchor: حجة التنوين أن اسم الفاعل فيه للحال

rows.speaker: من أضاف
rows.claim: The construct reading drops tanwīn as in عارضا مستقبل أوديتهم; it may also describe someone who has already warned, like ضارب زيد أمس.
rows.anchor: ومن أضاف استخف فحذف التنوين كما حذف من قوله

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains yāʾ in both connection and pause in يسر and جابوا الصخر.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: يسري* [الفجر/ 4] بالياء وصل أو وقف، وجابوا الصخر بالوادي

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ retains yāʾ in connection but drops it at a pause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع بالياء في الوصل، وبغير ياء في الوقف

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These four readers omit yāʾ in both connection and pause; Abū ʿUbaydah says al-Kisāʾī formerly retained it before returning to omission.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي: يسر بغير ياء في وصل

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Reports differ about Abū ʿAmr: one says he omits yāʾ in both positions, another says he retains it only when connecting, and another says he adds it within an āyah but pauses without it at the verse end.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو فيما روى عباس قال: سألت أبا عمرو فقرأ: يسر* جزم

rows.speaker: اليزيدي
rows.claim: Al-Yazīdī says connection has yāʾ and silent pause omits it, following the written form.
rows.anchor: وقال اليزيدي: الوصل بالياء والسكت بغير ياء على الكتاب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers use the verbal forms فك رقبة or أطعم, with رقبة in the accusative; Abū ʿAmr's transmitters report minor differences over the two forms and their attachment.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وأبو عمرو والكسائي: فك رقبة أو أطعم

rows.speaker: عاصم وابن عامر ونافع وحمزة
rows.claim: These readers use the verbal noun إطعام alongside فك رقبة.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وابن عامر ونافع وحمزة: فك رقبة أو إطعام

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan identifies the steep path as Hell.
rows.anchor: قال أبو رجاء سمعت الحسن يقول: فلا اقتحم العقبة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatādah calls the steep path a severe trial and says people cross it through obedience to God.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة: فلا اقتحم العقبة أنها قحمة شديدة

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abū ʿUbaydah says the person failed to cross the path in worldly life, then takes freeing a captive or feeding as its explanation.
rows.anchor: أبو عبيدة: فلا اقتحم العقبة: فلم يقتحم العقبة في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the verbal-noun reading, an omitted اقتحام is required: otherwise the sentence equates the path itself with the event of freeing a captive, unlike the intended explanatory relation.
rows.anchor: لا بد من تقدير هذا المحذوف لأنه لا يخلو من أن تقدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here لا means لم, so it need not be repeated; repetition in another verse is comparable to repeated لم.
rows.anchor: ومعنى: فلا اقتحم العقبة لم يقتحمها، وإذا كانت لا* بمعنى لم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being among the believers is necessary for the freeing and other good deeds to benefit, because disbelief cancels their reward.
rows.anchor: فإنه إن لم يكن منهم لم ينفعه قربة لإحباط الكفر لها

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan calls one of the two readings better and says it is the one he reads; he also allows describing a day as hungry, as one describes a night as sleeping.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الحسن: هي أجود من الأخرى وبها نقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verbal reading may explain the challenge through its actions; an explanatory clause need not copy the nominal-predicate construction in other examples, and meaning can link the clauses.
rows.anchor: ومن قال: فك رقبة أو أطعم في يوم ذي مسغبة [البلد/ 13، 14]، فإنه يجوز

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr, ʿĀṣim, and Ibn ʿĀmir open the endings in this sūrah, al-Layl, and al-Ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر: بفتح أواخر آي هذه السورة

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī uses imālah throughout these endings and the endings of al-Layl and al-Ḍuḥā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بإضجاع ذلك كله، وإضجاع أواخر سورة والليل

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamzah varies the endings: he inclines ḍuḥāhā but opens talāhā and ṭaḥāhā, while inclining the remaining forms, including sajā and daḥāhā.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة: وضحاها* [1] كسرا، ويفتح تلاها

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nāfiʿ has several transmissions: some make the endings intermediate, while Warsh and Qālūn are also reported to open them all; another report opens only talāhā and inclines the rest.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع ذلك كله بين الفتح والكسر. وقال خلف عن إسحاق

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported as using intermediate imālah, while ʿAbbās reports fully inclined forms for selected endings; other transmissions describe his treatment across verse endings.
rows.anchor: وقال اليزيدي عن أبي عمرو: ذلك كله بين الفتح والكسر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Imālah is licensed where the alif behaves as one originating in yāʾ, as in derived verbs and nouns; an alif from wāw, such as العصا, normally resists it.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت هذه في حكم الانقلاب عن الياء أجروا الألف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rare inclined examples with an alif from wāw are too uncommon to challenge the general pattern.
rows.anchor: فذلك من القلة بحيث لا يسوغ الاعتراض به

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو ونافع
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr is reported with a fully inclined ending, while Nāfiʿ and another transmission from Abū ʿAmr are reported with intermediate or inclined forms; Abū ʿAlī refers back to the earlier discussion.
rows.anchor: أبو عمرو: يكسرها في رواية عباس، نافع: بين الكسر والفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The vocalization ṣurhunna follows the normal pattern for a transitive doubled verb; the rāʾ takes ḍamma by vowel harmony with the following hāʾ.
rows.anchor: وأما "صرهن" بضم الصاد فعلى الباب؛ أعني: ضم عين يفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form ṣurhunna can derive from ṣarā, 'to restrain or cut off'; the same root describes milk withheld in a sheep's udder and water held in place.
rows.anchor: وأما "فصرهن" فهذا فعلهن6 من صرى يصري: إذا حبس وقطع

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر والزهري
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar and al-Zuhrī read جزءا as جزا by easing the hamza, then carrying a pause form into connection; pause permits several realizations, including lengthening or gemination.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة أبي جعفر والزهري: "جزا"

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والزهري
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyab and al-Zuhrī read صفوان with fatḥa on fāʾ; the pattern فعْلان is common in descriptions and verbal nouns but possible in other nouns too.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة سعيد بن المسيب والزهري: "كمثل صفوان عليه تراب"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pattern فعْلان generally signals motion or lightness in descriptions and verbal nouns, though examples such as صفوان show that it can also occur in ordinary nouns.
rows.anchor: والمعنى -في الوصف والمصدر جميعا من هذا المثال- الحركة والخفة

rows.speaker: الزهري ومسلم بن جندب
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī and Muslim ibn Jundub read ولا تَيَمَّموا with ḍamma on tāʾ and kasra on mīm; its several verb forms all mean to intend or seek.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة "30و" الزهري ومسلم بن جندب5: "ولا تيمموا الخبيث"6

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The root أ م م means intending; الإمام is what one aims at or relies on, and الأمة can mean an intended path, as in the cited verse.
rows.anchor: الأم: القصد، ومثله الأمت، ومنه الإمام لأنه المقصود المعتمد

rows.speaker: الأصمعي
rows.claim: Al-Aṣmaʿī reports the form غار for 'sank or disappeared'; the source says this sense differs from the interpretation that means going to al-Ghawr.
rows.anchor: ورواية الأصمعي: غار، على ما مضى، وليس المعنى على ما قدمنا واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The form تغمضوا can be transferred from intransitive غمض to transitive أغمضه, meaning that someone else causes the overlooking.
rows.anchor: وأما "تغمضوا فيه" فيكون منقولا من غمض هو وأغمضه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jinnī reads أغفلنا as 'We found him heedless,' not 'We made him heedless': if it expressed causation, the following consequence would normally use fa, not wa.
rows.anchor: ولو كان أغفلنا هنا منقولا من غفل -أي: منعناه وصددناه-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the transferred reading, the wording can mean finding people treating the poor offering as something they have already overlooked, supported by other examples of أفعل meaning 'find in a state.'
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن الناس يجدونهم قد غمضوا فيه، فيكون من أفعلت الشيء وجدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another sense of تغمضوا is to be drawn toward the inferior gift by desire until it seems acceptable; al-Zuhrī's report can mean deliberately closing one's judgment to its defect.
rows.anchor: والآخر: أن يكون "تغمضوا فيه" أي: إلا أن تدخلوا فيه وتجذبوا إليه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads واتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا with kasra on qāf and a still yāʾ; poetry attests to the unusual stilling.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الحسن: "اتقوا الله وذروا ما بقي من الربا "5 بكسر القاف

rows.speaker: أبو السمال
rows.claim: Abū al-Sammāl reads ما بقي من الربو with ḍamma on bāʾ and final still wāw; the author calls this doubly irregular in vowel sequence and word-final sound.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك ما رواه ابن مجاهد عن أبي زيد عن أبي السمال: أنه كان يقرأ: "ما بقي من الربو"1

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The final wāw after ḍamma is unattested in nouns except the anomalous Tayy form ذو, which also changes its wāw outside the nominative.
rows.anchor: والآخر: وقوع الواو بعد الضمة في آخر الاسم، وهذا شيء لم يأت إلا في الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The present form يستغفر narrates an anticipated event as though occurring now, a common Arabic device also used for past and future scenes.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: أما "يستغفر" فعلى حكاية الحال، كقولك: كان زيد سيقوم

rows.speaker: عكرمة وزر بن حبيش وعمرو بن عبيد
rows.claim: The standard reading passivizes خُلّفوا, while these readers use خَلَفوا to mean they stayed behind; a further group reads خالفوا, meaning they opposed and thus remained behind.
rows.anchor: وقرأ: "خلفوا" -بفتح الخاء واللام خفيفة- عكرمة وزر بن حبيش

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وعلي بن الحسين وجعفر بن محمد وأبو عبد الرحمن السلمي
rows.claim: This group reads خالفوا; the author says its sense converges with 'stayed behind,' since their opposition resulted in remaining there.
rows.anchor: قرأ: "خالفوا" أبو جعفر محمد بن علي وعلي بن الحسين

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن قسيط المكي
rows.claim: Ibn Qusayṭ al-Makkī reads من أنفسكم, meaning 'from your finest people,' since النفس can denote what is most excellent.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة عبد الله بن قسيط المكي: "لقد جاءكم رسول من أنفسكم"

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب وعروة بن الزبير وأبو جعفر وجعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: These readers say ونادى نوح ابنه; ʿUrwah also reports ابنهَا, identifying the son as the wife's, while al-Suddī's ابناه is a lamenting vocative and Ibn ʿAbbās has a jussive hāʾ.
rows.anchor: قراءة علي بن أبي طالب -عليه السلام- وعروة5 بن الزبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shortened ابنه means ابنها, with the wife's previously mentioned reference allowing deletion of the alif; the long form ابناه is a vocative lament, while the jussive form reflects an Azd dialect.
rows.anchor: أما "ابنه" فإنه أراد ابنها، كما يروى عن عروة فيما قرأ: "ابنها"

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: A report from al-Aʿmash lightens the yāʾ in الجودي; although rare outside poetry, the author supports it with poetic and prose examples.
rows.anchor: ومن قراءة الأعمش بخلاف: "على الجودي" خفيف

rows.speaker: محمد بن زياد الأعرابي
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn Ziyād al-Aʿrābī reads فَضَحِكَت with a fatḥa; Ibn al-Aʿrābī explains ضحك as menstruation and cites two poetic witnesses.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة محمد بن زياد5 الأعرابي: "فضحكت"6 فتحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The referenced form may be a plural of عشوة, meaning darkness, with its separate portions motivating the plural.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون جمع عشوة: أي ظلاما، وجمعه لتفرق أجزائه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan's variant دم كدب derives from a word for the pale marks on young people's nails, describing blood patterned on the shirt.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: أصل هذا من الكدب؛ وهو الفوف؛ يعني: البياض الذي يخرج

rows.speaker: أبو الطفيل والجحدري وابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: These readers, also reported from al-Ḥasan, say يا بشري; the author calls this a widespread dialectal form and explains the yāʾ as replacing an expected kasra before possessive yāʾ.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة أبي الطفيل1 والجحدري وابن أبي إسحاق ورويت عن الحسن: "يا بشري"2

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif of the dual is not similarly changed to yāʾ because that would collapse the nominative form with accusative and genitive; a consonant change is weightier than a vowel change.
rows.anchor: ومن قلب هذه الألف لوقوع هذه الياء بعدها ياء لم يفعل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative parses the bāʾ as linking to an omitted predicate and takes the noun as the price paid: the phrase means the person is not worth that amount.
rows.anchor: فيكون "الشري" هنا يراد به المفعول به؛ أي: الثمن المشترى به

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar reports hearing a reader say عتى حين, asks who taught him, then instructs Ibn Masʿūd to teach Quraysh Arabic rather than Hudhayl's dialect.
rows.anchor: ما روي عن عمر أنه سمع رجلا يقرأ: "عتى حين"5، فقال: من أقرأك؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The consonants in عتى and حتى can interchange because their articulation points are close; the more commonly used form is preferable, though the variant is permissible.
rows.anchor: العرب تبدل أحد هذين الحرفين من صاحبه لتقاربهما في المخرج

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reads أعصر عنبا; the standard أعصر خمرا anticipates what the grapes will become, a future state named as though present.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن مسعود: "إني أراني أعصر عنبا"7

rows.speaker: عكرمة والجحدري
rows.claim: ʿIkrimah and al-Jaḥdarī read فيسقى ربه خمرا, making the cupbearer's good outcome parallel to the other prisoner's punishment.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة عكرمة والجحدري: "فيسقى ربه خمرا"3

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن عمر وعكرمة ومجاهد والضحاك وقتادة
rows.claim: These readers say وادكر بعد أمه, meaning after forgetfulness; al-Ashhab al-ʿUqaylī instead reads بعد إمة, meaning after a blessing.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن عباس وابن عمر بخلاف وعكرمة ومجاهد بخلاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأمه means forgetfulness, while الإمة means a blessing, so the two readings give different accounts of what followed Joseph's rescue.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الفتح: "الأمه": النسيان، أمه الرجل يأمه أمها: أي نسي

rows.speaker: عيسى والأعرج وجعفر بن محمد
rows.claim: These readers pronounce يُعْصَرون with a yāʾ and open ṣād; it can mean receiving rain or rescue, while Ibn ʿAbbās explains the rescue through pressing grapes or oils.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة عيسى والأعرج وجعفر بن محمد: "وفيه يعصرون"8

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says يعصرون means they press grapes or oils; the poem's عصرة means relief or rescue for someone in distress.
rows.anchor: وروينا عن ابن عباس: أي يعصرون من الكرم والأدهان

rows.speaker: علقمة ويحيى
rows.claim: ʿAlqamah and Yaḥyā read رُدِت إلينا with kasra on rāʾ; this is a rare pure-kasra form of a doubled verb, alongside the more common ḍamma and intermediate pronunciation.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة علقمة ويحيى: "ردت إلينا3" بكسر الراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For hollow verbs, first-vowel kasra is most common, followed by a mixed vowel and then pure ḍamma; the cited poems attest the rarer forms and dialects.
rows.anchor: وأما المعتل العين، فأقوى اللغات فيه كسر أوله، نحو: قيل وبيع

rows.speaker: الجحدري
rows.claim: Al-Jaḥdarī reads تزوار in the ifʿāl pattern; the author notes that this pattern usually describes colors or visible defects but has other attestations.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الجحدري: "تزوار3".

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because ifʿāl is intransitive, the object خليلًا in the cited poem depends on an implied verb such as serve, care for, or replace.
rows.anchor: وخليلا عندنا منصوب بفعل مضمر يدل عليه "مقتو"، وذلك أن افعل لا يتعدى

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads وتقلبهم as an accusative verbal noun governed by an implied 'We see' or 'We witness,' in keeping with the surrounding observable scenes.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة2 الحسن: "وتقلبهم3"، بفتح التاء والقاف

rows.speaker: ابن محيصن
rows.claim: Ibn Muḥayṣin alone assimilates the thāʾ of ثلات into the tāʾ of رابعهم; their nearby articulation points license the assimilation despite the preceding alif.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة ابن محيصن: "ثلات رابعهم كلبهم7"

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr alone has a report with fatḥa on the mīm of خمسة; the author attributes it to transmitted usage, perhaps following the preceding عشرة.
rows.anchor: إلا ابن كثير وحده في رواية حسن بن محمد2 عن شبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unusual vowel should not be dismissed as poetic necessity: Arabic place names can have variant forms, as the report about ركك and ركا illustrates.
rows.anchor: أتعرف رككا هذا؟ فقال: قد كان ههنا ماء يسمى "ركا"

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads ولا تعد عينيك, a causative of 'your eyes passed beyond,' meaning turn your eyes away from the worldly adornment.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الحسن: "ولا تعد عينيك9"

rows.speaker: عمرو بن فائد
rows.claim: ʿAmr ibn Fāʾid reads من أغفلنا as 'one whom We found heedless,' not 'one whom We caused to be heedless'; the author defends this as an established أفعل usage and answers the theological objection.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة عمرو بن فائد: "من أغفلنا قلبه2"

rows.speaker: مجاهد وحميد بن قيس
rows.claim: Mujāhid and Ḥumayd ibn Qays read خاسر الدنيا والآخرة as a circumstantial accusative: the person turns away already losing both worlds.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة مجاهد وحميد بن قيس: "خاسر الدنيا والآخرة"3

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The standard خسر الدنيا والآخرة is a clause replacing انقلب على وجهه; explanatory clauses can likewise replace a conditional answer, as in the cited Qur'anic and poetic examples.
rows.anchor: تكون هذه الجملة بدلا من قوله

rows.speaker: الزهري
rows.claim: Al-Zuhrī alone is reported to lighten the doubled bāʾ in الدواب, a form the author judges weak in both analogy and transmission.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة الزهري: "والدواب"2، خفيفة الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lengthening the alif compensates for the adjacent identical consonants, much like giving it the effect of a vowel; the light reading is not otherwise known in transmission.
rows.anchor: ويدل على أن زيادة المد في الألف جار مجرى تحريكها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The variant قيعات may be a plural of قيعة, like ديمة/ديمات, or a plural of قاع, like نار/نيرة; it may also be lengthened قيعة in poetic pronunciation.
rows.anchor: وقد يجوز أن يكون قيعات بالتاء جمع قيعة، كديمة وديمات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If قيعات is a plural, it evokes many separate patches, as in the poem describing foam scattered across lowlands.
rows.anchor: فهو كقول الآخر: كأن بالقيعات من رغاها

rows.speaker: طلحة بن مصرف
rows.claim: Ṭalḥah ibn Muṣarrif reads سَناء برقه with a long alif: سناء means honor, which metaphorically conveys exceptional brightness; the common short form سنا means light.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة طلحة بن مصرف: "سناء برقه"3

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر يزيد
rows.claim: Abū Jaʿfar Yazīd reads يُذْهِب with ḍamma on yāʾ, making the lightning remove sight; the bāʾ emphasizes the verb's transitive force.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة أبي جعفر يزيد: "يذهب"5، بضم الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The bāʾ in يذهب بالأبصار is not empty addition: it reinforces transitivity, or the phrase can mean the lightning almost twists the eyes away or seizes them.
rows.anchor: ولا ترين الباء في: {يذهب بالأبصار} مزيدة زيادة ساذجة

rows.speaker: علي والحسن وابن أبي إسحاق
rows.claim: ʿAlī, al-Ḥasan in one report, and Ibn Abī Isḥāq read إنما كان قول المؤمنين with nominative قول; the community's reading uses accusative القول.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قراءة علي عليه السلام والحسن بخلاف، وابن أبي إسحاق: "إنما كان قول المؤمنين"4

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative is stronger because أن يقولوا is more definite than قول المؤمنين and therefore better suited as kāna's subject; nominative الخزي is explained by إلا affirming the already known subject of the sentence.
rows.anchor: أقوى القراءتين إعرابا ما عليه الجماعة من نصب "القول"
